items.stem: Explain how Bt toxin kills insects and how Bt cotton is produced.
items.answer: Bacillus thuringiensis forms protein crystals containing an inactive protoxin. In the alkaline pH of the insect gut the crystals are solubilised and the toxin is activated; it binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing swelling and lysis, and the insect dies. Bt cotton: the specific cry genes (cryIAc, cryIIAb for bollworms; cryIAb for corn borer) are isolated from B. thuringiensis and incorporated into cotton plants, which then make the toxin.
items.markingKey: 3 marks mechanism; 2 marks production.

items.stem: Describe how genetically engineered human insulin is produced. Why is it preferred over insulin from animal sources?
items.answer: Insulin is made of two short polypeptide chains A and B linked by disulphide bridges; in humans it is synthesised as proinsulin with an extra C peptide. Eli Lilly (1983) prepared two DNA sequences for chains A and B, introduced them into plasmids of E. coli, produced the chains separately, extracted them and combined them by creating disulphide bonds to form human insulin. It does not cause allergic reactions to foreign proteins and can be produced in large quantities to meet demand.
items.markingKey: 3 marks production; 2 marks advantages.

Reason (R): The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with ADA deficiency.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Lymphocytes are not immortal, so periodic infusion is needed; introducing the gene into early embryonic cells could be a permanent cure. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A transgenic crop has these features: reduces use of chemical pesticides; produces an insecticidal protein; contains a cry gene. Identify the crop. Give a reason.
items.answer: Bt cotton
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Bt cotton; 1 mark: the features reduces use of chemical pesticides; produces an insecticidal protein; contains a cry gene are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events in the action of Bt toxin: cells swell and lyse, insect eats Bt toxin crystals, insect dies. Give a reason.
items.answer: insect eats Bt toxin crystals → cells swell and lyse → insect dies
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order insect eats Bt toxin crystals → cells swell and lyse → insect dies; 1 mark for the reason: Toxin causes lysis of gut cells.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Transgenic mice are being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine.
Reason (R): GEAC was set up by the United Nations.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: GEAC is a committee set up by the Indian Government.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Insulin from animal sources never caused allergies.”
items.answer: Animal insulin caused allergy or other reactions to the foreign protein in some patients.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Animal insulin caused allergy or other reactions to the foreign protein in some patients.

items.stem:
A transgenic crop has these features: reduces use of chemical pesticides; contains a cry gene; produces an insecticidal protein.
(i) Identify the crop. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were RNAi tobacco? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Bt cotton (ii) protects against bollworms (iii) silences parasite mRNA; resists Meloidogyne incognita
items.markingKey: (i) Bt cotton – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: protects against bollworms – 1 mark. (iii) for RNAi tobacco: contains nematode-specific genes; produces dsRNA in host cells; silences parasite mRNA – 1 mark each for any two.

items.answer: chains A and B made separately in E. coli and joined by disulphide bonds

items.stem: Classify each of the following as ethical concern about GMOs or Indian regulatory or legal step: amendment of the Indian Patents Bill, biopiracy of indigenous resources, use of animals causing suffering, unpredictable effects when introduced into ecosystems.
items.answer: amendment of the Indian Patents Bill – Indian regulatory or legal step; biopiracy of indigenous resources – ethical concern about GMOs; use of animals causing suffering – ethical concern about GMOs; unpredictable effects when introduced into ecosystems – ethical concern about GMOs.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: amendment of the Indian Patents Bill – Indian regulatory or legal step; biopiracy of indigenous resources – ethical concern about GMOs; use of animals causing suffering – ethical concern about GMOs; unpredictable effects when introduced into ecosystems – ethical concern about GMOs.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of steps in gene therapy for ADA deficiency: grown in culture, lymphocytes taken from patient's blood, lymphocytes returned to patient, functional ADA cDNA introduced using a retroviral vector. Give a reason.
items.answer: lymphocytes taken from patient's blood → grown in culture → functional ADA cDNA introduced using a retroviral vector → lymphocytes returned to patient
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order lymphocytes taken from patient's blood → grown in culture → functional ADA cDNA introduced using a retroviral vector → lymphocytes returned to patient; 1 mark for the reason: Periodic infusion is needed.

items.stem: Rosie, the first transgenic cow (1997), produced milk containing 2.4 g of human alpha-lactalbumin per litre. Siddharth calculates the amount of this protein in 20 L of such milk. What is it, and why is this milk better for human babies?
items.answer: 48 g; it is nutritionally a more balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk
items.markingKey: Mass = 2.4 g L⁻¹ × 20 L = 48 g (1); human alpha-lactalbumin makes the milk nutritionally more balanced for human babies (1).

items.stem: Define the term “ADA deficiency”.
items.answer: A disorder caused by deletion of the gene for adenosine deaminase, an enzyme crucial for the immune system.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a disorder caused by deletion of the gene for adenosine deaminase, an enzyme crucial for the immune system.
